svg.text: INSTRUCTIONAL MOCKUP — NOT A LIVE CAPTURE OR RESULT
Trust the checked root in that profile only
Your Windows host · Firefox SONIC TLS Practice profile · Certificate Manager
Firefox · SONIC TLS Practice | about:preferences#privacy — Certificate Manager
Certificate Manager
Your Certificates People Servers Authorities
Import → Documents / SONIC-TLS / root.crt
View → compare SHA-256 certificate fingerprint to CA console
Only the checked practice root identifies websites in this profile.
EXPECTED RESULT / SIMULATED CLUE — CHECK YOUR OWN MACHINE
The practice page opens without a trust warning in this profile; its certificate names
app.example.mil and uses the practice issuer.
FOLLOW THE NUMBERED INSTRUCTIONS IN THE LESSON
1. In the practice Firefox window, type about:preferences#privacy in the address bar. Scroll to
Certificates and select View Certificates. Labels may vary slightly by version.
2. Open the Authorities tab, click Import, and choose Documents\SONIC-TLS\
oot.crt.
3. Use View to inspect the certificate. Compare its SHA-256 fingerprint with openssl x509 -in ~/tls-
ca/root.crt -noout -fingerprint -sha256 on the CA console before accepting trust.
4. Only after the match, allow this CA to identify websites in this disposable practice profile. Never
enable trust for an unknown CA or import the intermediate as a root.
5. Then open https://app.example.mil. Use the padlock/site information control, Connection secure, More
Information or View Certificate to inspect the leaf SAN, issuer and dates.
No real private key, real certificate result, production access or DoD endorsement is shown.
